title: 3 x 3 matrix multiplication, number of multiplications
statement: Find a bilinear algorithm that multiplies two 3 x 3 matrices with non-commuting entries using as few multiplications as possible: a decomposition of the matrix multiplication tensor <3,3,3> into R products. Laderman's 1976 algorithm uses 23; the lower bound is 19 (Bläser 2003). Any field is accepted.
submission: JSON {"field": F, "terms": [[U, V, W], ...]}: F is "Q", "Q(i)" or "GF(p)"; U is N x M, V is M x P and W is N x P, lists of rows; entries are integers or strings "a/b" (over Q(i) also pairs [re, im]); product r is (sum U_r[i][j] A[i][j]) (sum V_r[j][k] B[j][k]) and C[i][k] = sum_r W_r[i][k] times product r.
score: R, the number of multiplications (smaller is better)

best_known.source: <3x3x3:23>: J. D. Laderman, Bull. AMS 82 (1976) 126-128, in A. Sedoglavic's catalogue of fast matrix multiplication algorithms (fmm.univ-lille.fr, version 1c55fea); read 9 Nov 2026

provenance.keeper: A. Sedoglavic, Yet another catalogue of fast matrix multiplication algorithms

bound.source: M. Bläser, On the complexity of the multiplication of matrices of small formats, J. Complexity 19 (2003)
